## Diagnostic study

It is important to note that to run this series of experiments, one of the files '02_reorder'
or 'RMaCzek_test.R' should be run completely. The simulated annealing code is looking for patterns in how trait changes distribute across tree tips. In evolutionary biology, this concept is called phylogenetic signal—the statistical tendency for related species to resemble one another more than they resemble species drawn at random from the tree.


## phylogenetic signal

On real biological datasets phylosignal can definitively prove whether the optimized layout highlights true evolutionary constraints or just arbitrary numeric sorting.
whether closely related species tend to resemble each other in their trait values more than expected by chance. This output contains two indices:
Blomberg's K: measures whether trait similarity follows the phylogenetic tree.
Abouheif's Cmean: another measure of phylogenetic autocorrelation, sensitive to trait clustering among related taxa.

```{r}
# install.packages("phylosignal")
library(phylosignal)
library(phylobase)

# Merge the tree and traits into a unified S4 object
p4d <- phylo4d(optimized_tree, traits)

# Calculate standard biological indices like Blomberg's K and Abouheif's Cmean
signal_metrics <- phyloSignal(p4d, methods = c("K", "Cmean"))
print(signal_metrics)

# Check the biological signal for Trait 1
signal <- phylosig(my_tree, traits[, "Trait3"], method = "lambda")
print(signal)
```

## Tanglegrams

If you want to evaluate how heavily the tree's fixed evolutionary branches are constraining the trait sorting, you can use a tanglegram (a visual tool that draws two trees facing each other with lines connecting matching tips)

```{r}
# install.packages("phylogram")
library(dendextend)
library(phylogram) # Provides direct phylo -> dendrogram conversion

# Convert directly without using intermediate as.hclust steps
dend_orig <- as.dendrogram(compute.brlen(my_tree))

optimized_ultra <- force.ultrametric(optimized_tree, method = "nnls")
dend_opt <- as.dendrogram(optimized_ultra)

# Plot tanglegram
tanglegram(dend_orig, dend_opt, main_left = "Original", main_right = "Optimized",
           fast = TRUE, highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE)

```

## Tree and visual analysis

To experimentally construct and save a tree with the absolute least cost, we can build a new tree topology from scratch using data-driven clustering methods (Hierarchical Clustering and Neighbor-Joining) driven purely by the trait matrix, and then run the simulated annealing algorithm on that to find the ultimate optimal node rotations.By building a tree using hclust() or nj(), we allow similar tips to cluster together immediately. The algorithm groups Tip1 and Tip100 right next to each other on a tiny local node because it doesn't care about their evolutionary past.
For even better unconstrained cost, use the global optimization from '02_reorder'.

```{r}
# Make sure ape is loaded for tree handling
library(ape)

## =============================================================================
## 1. BUILD TRAIT-DRIVEN TOPOLOGIES (Phenetic Trees)
## =============================================================================

# Compute the 6-dimensional Euclidean distance matrix between all tips
trait_dist <- dist(traits)

# Method A: Hierarchical Clustering (UPGMA / Average Linkage)
# This groups tips purely by overall trait profile similarity
hc_cluster <- hclust(trait_dist, method = "average")
trait_tree_hc <- as.phylo(hc_cluster)

# Method B: Neighbor-Joining (NJ)
# A standard phylogenetic algorithm, but here used entirely on trait distances
trait_tree_nj <- nj(trait_dist)

## =============================================================================
## 2. OPTIMIZE THE UNCONSTRAINED TREE
## =============================================================================
cat("--- Optimizing the Unconstrained Trait Tree ---\n")

# We use the Hierarchical Clustering tree as our starting unconstrained topology
# and let simulated annealing find the best leaf arrangement allowed by it.
unconstrained_result <- anneal_tree(
    trait_tree_hc,
    traits,
    max_iter = 200000,
    temperature = 10,
    patience = 10000
)

absolute_best_tree <- unconstrained_result$tree

## =============================================================================
## 3. CALCULATE THE THEORETICAL ABSOLUTE FLOOR (Unconstrained Path)
## =============================================================================
# As a baseline, what if there was no tree structure at all? 
# We can project the traits to PC1 and sort them to approximate the optimal TSP path.
pca_sort_order <- names(sort(prcomp(traits, scale. = TRUE)$x[, 1]))
X_spatial <- traits[pca_sort_order, , drop = FALSE]
theoretical_floor <- sum(sqrt(rowSums((X_spatial[-1, , drop=FALSE] - X_spatial[-nrow(X_spatial), , drop=FALSE])^2)))

## =============================================================================
## 4. COMPARE COSTS & SAVE
## =============================================================================
cat("\n=============================================\n")
cat("            EXPERIMENTAL COST REPORT         \n")
cat("=============================================\n")
cat("Original Evolutionary Tree Cost:        ", init_cost, "\n")
cat("OLO-Optimized Evolutionary Tree Cost:   ", result$cost, "\n")
cat("---------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Raw Hierarchical Cluster Tree Cost:     ", trait_cost(trait_tree_hc, traits), "\n")
cat("Raw Neighbor-Joining Tree Cost:          ", trait_cost(trait_tree_nj, traits), "\n")
cat("Optimized Unconstrained Tree Cost:      ", unconstrained_result$cost, "\n")
cat("---------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Theoretical TSP Floor (No Tree Control):", theoretical_floor, "\n")
cat("=============================================\n")

# Save absolute lowest-cost tree to a Newick file
write.tree(absolute_best_tree, file = "least_cost_trait_tree.tre")
cat("Saved the unconstrained optimal tree to 'least_cost_trait_tree.tre'\n")

## =============================================================================
## 5. VISUAL INSPECTION
## =============================================================================
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(optimized_tree, show.tip.label=FALSE, main="Best Evolutionary Tree")
plot(absolute_best_tree, show.tip.label=FALSE, main="Absolute Least Cost Tree")
```


When dealing with 6-dimensional trait data, it is hard to visualize the entire space at once. By running a Principal Component Analysis (PCA), we can compress those 6 traits into a single principal component ($PC_1$) that captures the maximum variance, and then map that variance directly onto the branches of both the original and optimized trees.

```{r}

# heal tree
optimized_tree <- sanitize_tree(optimized_tree)
# 1. Run PCA on the 6-dimensional trait matrix
# Scaling is recommended since traits are uniformly random but could vary in scale in real data
pca_result <- prcomp(traits, scale. = TRUE)

# 2. Extract the first Principal Component (PC1) as a named vector
pc1_values <- pca_result$x[, 1]
names(pc1_values) <- rownames(traits)

# 3. Compute ancestral states and map PC1 onto both topologies
map_original  <- contMap(my_tree, pc1_values, plot=FALSE)
map_optimized <- contMap(optimized_tree, pc1_values, plot=FALSE)

# 4. Plot side-by-side to inspect the OLO visual smoothing effect
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(map_original, sig=2, fsize=0.01, main="Original Tree (PC1 Color Map)")
plot(map_optimized, sig=2, fsize=0.01, main="OLO Optimized Tree (PC1 Color Map)")
```
The most intuitive way to validate an OLO optimization is to plot the tree right next to a full heatmap of all 6 raw traits. The phylo.heatmap function automatically reorders the rows of the trait matrix to match the exact plotting layout of the tree leaves.

```{r}
# Set up a two-panel plotting window
par(mfrow=c(1,2))

# Plot the original tree alongside its raw trait matrix layout
phylo.heatmap(my_tree, traits, 
              fsize=c(0.01, 0.8, 0.8), # Shrink tip labels to fit 100 tips
              labels=FALSE,            # Turn off tip text clutter
              main="Original Tree Trait Layout")

# Plot the OLO optimized tree alongside the exact same trait matrix
phylo.heatmap(optimized_tree, traits, 
              fsize=c(0.01, 0.8, 0.8), 
              labels=FALSE, 
              main="Optimized Tree Trait Layout")
```
this visualization allows us to inspect the intersection of evolutionary history (clades) and trait optimization. In a standard phylogenetic tree, tips that share a recent common ancestor sit next to each other. The OLO algorithm rotates nodes to optimize trait transitions without breaking these ancestral pairs:

```{r}
library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Build the base ggplot objects for both trees
p1 <- ggtree(my_tree) + ggtitle("Original Structure")
p2 <- ggtree(optimized_tree) + ggtitle("OLO Optimized Structure")

# 2. Overlay the 6-dimensional trait matrix as an aligned heatmap grid
# offset shifts the matrix away from the tips; width controls matrix thickness
plot_orig_heatmap <- gheatmap(p1, as.data.frame(traits), 
                              offset=0.1, 
                              width=0.6, 
                              colnames_position="top", 
                              colnames_angle=45, 
                              colnames_offset_y=1.2,
                              font.size=3) + 
                     scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name="Trait Value")

plot_opt_heatmap  <- gheatmap(p2, as.data.frame(traits), 
                              offset=0.1, 
                              width=0.6, 
                              colnames_position="top", 
                              colnames_angle=45, 
                              colnames_offset_y=1.2,
                              font.size=3) + 
                     scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name="Trait Value")

# 3. Print the plots to the active viewport device
print(plot_orig_heatmap)
# Open a new window or clear plot to view the second
print(plot_opt_heatmap)
```
## Neighbor Jump-Distance Distribution

Our optimization minimizes the total path distance between consecutive leaves. Looking at the total cost doesn't tell us if we solved the whole tree uniformly, or if we fixed 99 leaves but left one massive, catastrophic jump in the middle.We can calculate the specific vector of neighbor-to-neighbor Euclidean step distances:
$$d_i = \sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^{m} (X_{i+1, j} - X_{i, j})^2}$$
```{r}
# Function to extract raw step distances between adjacent tips
get_neighbor_distances <- function(tree, traits) {
    ord <- get_plot_order(tree)
    X <- traits[ord, , drop = FALSE]
    sqrt(rowSums((X[-1, , drop = FALSE] - X[-nrow(X), , drop = FALSE])^2))
}

dist_orig <- get_neighbor_distances(my_tree, traits)
dist_opt  <- get_neighbor_distances(optimized_tree, traits)

# Plot overlapping density distributions
plot(density(dist_orig), col="red", lwd=2, xlim=range(c(dist_orig, dist_opt)),
     main="Distribution of Trait 'Jumps' Between Adjacent Tips", xlab="Euclidean Distance Step")
lines(density(dist_opt), col="darkgreen", lwd=2)
legend("topright", legend=c("Original Tree", "OLO Optimized"), col=c("red", "darkgreen"), lty=1, lwd=2)

# Quantitative Summary Table
summary_stats <- rbind(
    Original = summary(dist_orig),
    Optimized = summary(dist_opt)
)
print(summary_stats)
```

## Trait-by-Trait Stress

Because the original data has 6 continuous dimensions, a basic distance calculation aggregates them all together. It is highly likely that the tree structure matches some traits perfectly while conflicting with others. We can isolate the variance contribution of each single trait.

```{r}
get_dimensional_stress <- function(tree, traits) {
    ord <- get_plot_order(tree)
    X <- traits[ord, , drop = FALSE]
    # Sum of absolute or squared differences per column
    colSums(abs(X[-1, , drop = FALSE] - X[-nrow(X), , drop = FALSE]))
}

stress_orig <- get_dimensional_stress(my_tree, traits)
stress_opt  <- get_dimensional_stress(optimized_tree, traits)

# Barplot comparison of individual traits
stress_matrix <- rbind(Original = stress_orig, Optimized = stress_opt)
barplot(stress_matrix, beside=TRUE, col=c("coral", "steelblue"),
        main="Stress Contribution per Individual Trait Dimension",
        ylab="Total Absolute Step Variance")
legend("topright", legend=rownames(stress_matrix), fill=c("coral", "steelblue"))
```
## Trait Space Trajectory Path (PCA Space Walk)

Instead of looking at the tree, we can look directly at the 6-dimensional trait space projected into 2D using your PCA results. By drawing a continuous path that connects the tips in their exact plotting order, we can visualize the OLO optimization as a path-smoothing problem (akin to the Traveling Salesperson Problem).

```{r}
# 1. Compute 2D PCA coordinates
pca_res <- prcomp(traits, scale. = TRUE)
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:2])

# 2. Extract plotting orders
ord_orig <- get_plot_order(my_tree)
ord_opt  <- get_plot_order(optimized_tree)

# 3. Set up side-by-side plots
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Plot Original Tree Path
plot(pca_df$PC1, pca_df$PC2, type = "p", col = "grey", pch = 19,
     xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2", main = "Original Path through Trait Space")
lines(pca_df$PC1[match(ord_orig, rownames(pca_df))], 
      pca_df$PC2[match(ord_orig, rownames(pca_df))], 
      col = "firebrick", lwd = 1.5)

# Plot Optimized Tree Path
plot(pca_df$PC1, pca_df$PC2, type = "p", col = "grey", pch = 19,
     xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2", main = "OLO Optimized Path through Trait Space")
lines(pca_df$PC1[match(ord_opt, rownames(pca_df))], 
      pca_df$PC2[match(ord_opt, rownames(pca_df))], 
      col = "dodgerblue", lwd = 1.5)
```

## Principal Component Cost Decomposition

A global Euclidean cost function aggregates all dimensions into a single scalar. This hides whether the optimizer is successfully smoothing all dimensions or selectively optimizing high-variance axes while leaving minor axes chaotic.By projecting the 6-dimensional traits into orthogonal PCA space, we can calculate the step-by-step leaf transition cost independently for each Principal Component ($PC_1$ through $PC_6$).

```{r}
# 1. Compute PCA on raw traits
pca_res <- prcomp(traits, scale. = TRUE)
PC_matrix <- pca_res$x

# 2. Function to compute total step distance for each individual PC axis
get_pc_dropped_costs <- function(tree, PC_data) {
    ord <- get_plot_order(tree)
    X_ordered <- PC_data[ord, , drop = FALSE]
    # Calculate absolute first-differences along each column
    colSums(abs(X_ordered[-1, , drop = FALSE] - X_ordered[-nrow(X_ordered), , drop = FALSE]))
}

cost_per_pc_orig <- get_pc_dropped_costs(my_tree, PC_matrix)
cost_per_pc_opt  <- get_pc_dropped_costs(optimized_tree, PC_matrix)

# 3. Plot the Scree Cost Breakdown
cost_bars <- rbind(Original = cost_per_pc_orig, Optimized = cost_per_pc_opt)
barplot(cost_bars, beside = TRUE, col = c("indianred1", "mediumpurple3"),
        main = "Optimization Cost Reduction per Principal Component",
        xlab = "Eigenaxis", ylab = "Absolute Path Distance")
legend("topright", legend = rownames(cost_bars), fill = c("indianred1", "mediumpurple3"))
```

## Kinetic Trajectory Acceleration in 2D PCA Space

When the 1D leaf layout path is mapped onto a 2D PCA biplot ($PC_1 \times PC_2$), a well-optimized tree should look like a smooth, continuous string with minimal directional changes. An unoptimized tree will look jagged, making sharp U-turns across the space.We can quantify this visual roughness by calculating the Kinetic Acceleration Vector ($\Delta^2 X_i$) at each leaf step position. Higher acceleration values indicate violent directional shifts in trait space.
$$\Delta^2 X_i = X_{i+1} - 2X_i + X_{i-1}$$

```{r}
compute_path_acceleration <- function(tree, PC_data) {
    ord <- get_plot_order(tree)
    # Extract coordinates for the first two principal components
    X_2d <- PC_data[ord, 1:2]
    
    # Compute first difference (velocity vectors)
    v <- diff(X_2d)
    # Compute second difference (acceleration vectors)
    a <- diff(v)
    
    # Return the magnitude of acceleration at each step
    rowSums(a^2)
}

accel_orig <- compute_path_acceleration(my_tree, PC_matrix)
accel_opt  <- compute_path_acceleration(optimized_tree, PC_matrix)

# Plot acceleration magnitudes along the leaf index sequence
plot(accel_orig, type = "l", col = "salmon", log = "y", lwd = 1.5,
     xlab = "Leaf Chain Index Step (2 to N-1)", ylab = "Acceleration Magnitude (Log Scale)",
     main = "Path Kinetic Instability Profile")
lines(accel_opt, col = "cadetblue", lwd = 1.5)
legend("topright", legend = c("Original (High Inertia)", "Optimized (Smooth Trajectory)"), 
       col = c("salmon", "cadetblue"), lty = 1, lwd = 2)
```
```{r}
accel_opt_new  <- compute_path_acceleration(absolute_best_tree, PC_matrix)
plot(accel_opt_new, type = "l", col = "salmon", log = "y", lwd = 1.5,
     xlab = "Leaf Chain Index Step (2 to N-1)", ylab = "Acceleration Magnitude (Log Scale)",
     main = "Path Kinetic Instability Profile")
```

## Interactive tree + trait heatmap (Plotly)

The static panels above are useful, but it is hard to explore the interplay between clades and trait sorting by printing one fixed layout. This section defines a self-contained function, `interactive_tree_viz()`, that renders an **interactive Plotly htmlwidget**:

- a rectangular phylogram on the left with an aligned 6-trait heatmap on the right;
- hover anywhere: tips, internal nodes, and heatmap cells all show details;
- **click any internal-node diamond to flip (rotate) its two child clades**, which reorders only the leaves, preserving the topology exactly;
- a button toggles a second view with three aligned panels: the tree, the **species names**, and the **values of a selected trait**, with one dot per tip and dotted guide lines (a `plot_phylo_composite()`-style layout);
- an embedded **OLO (Bar-Joseph et al. 2001) optimal leaf ordering**, computed with tree-constrained rotations, plus a *Reset* and an *Apply OLO-optimal order* button;
- a live **adjacent-trait-distance readout** recomputed after every rotation;
- the (possibly reordered) tree is returned from R and can optionally be written to a Newick file;
- the output file name is a user-supplied argument (`output_file`), so the same function can be used for any tree/trait pair.

```{r interactive-tree-viz-function}
# =============================================================================
# interactive_tree_viz()
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plotly-based interactive visualization of an ape phylo tree + trait heatmap.
#   - Tree (rectangular phylogram) on the left, aligned trait heatmap on right
#   - Hover tips / internal nodes / heatmap cells for details
#   - Click an internal-node diamond to flip (rotate) its two child clades
#     without changing the topology
#   - Optional OLO (Bar-Joseph et al. 2001) optimal leaf ordering before plot,
#     with a button to restore the OLO-optimal order after manual edits
#   - A button toggles a second view: tree + species names + values of a
#     selected trait (one aligned panel per element, plot_phylo_composite-style)
#   - Output: a standalone interactive HTML file (plotly.js htmlwidget)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Self-contained OLO helpers (suffixed _2 to avoid clobbering the project's
# versions in 02_reorder.Rmd -- identical algorithm)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
get_children_list_2 <- function(phy) {
  n_tip  <- length(phy$tip.label)
  n_node <- phy$Nnode
  children <- vector("list", n_tip + n_node)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(phy$edge))) {
    p  <- phy$edge[i, 1]
    ch <- phy$edge[i, 2]
    children[[p]] <- c(children[[p]], ch)
  }
  children
}

olo_phylo_2 <- function(phy, d) {
  n_tip <- length(phy$tip.label)
  if (!is.matrix(d)) d <- as.matrix(d)
  stopifnot(nrow(d) == n_tip, ncol(d) == n_tip)
  children <- get_children_list_2(phy)
  memo <- vector("list", n_tip + phy$Nnode)
  dp <- function(node) {
    if (!is.null(memo[[node]])) return(memo[[node]])
    kids <- children[[node]]
    if (is.null(kids)) {
      res <- list(leaves = node,
                  table = matrix(0, 1, 1, dimnames = list(node, node)))
      memo[[node]] <<- res
      return(res)
    }
    if (length(kids) != 2) {
      stop("Node ", node, " has ", length(kids),
           " children; tree must be fully bifurcating (resolve with ape::multi2di).")
    }
    left  <- dp(kids[1])
    right <- dp(kids[2])
    Lleaves <- left$leaves;  Rleaves <- right$leaves
    LT <- left$table;        RT <- right$table
    L_full <- matrix(Inf, length(Lleaves), length(Lleaves),
                     dimnames = list(Lleaves, Lleaves))
    if (length(Lleaves) == 1) L_full[1, 1] <- 0 else {
      L_full[rownames(LT), colnames(LT)] <- LT
      L_full[colnames(LT), rownames(LT)] <- t(LT)
    }
    R_full <- matrix(Inf, length(Rleaves), length(Rleaves),
                     dimnames = list(Rleaves, Rleaves))
    if (length(Rleaves) == 1) R_full[1, 1] <- 0 else {
      R_full[rownames(RT), colnames(RT)] <- RT
      R_full[colnames(RT), rownames(RT)] <- t(RT)
    }
    tab  <- matrix(Inf, length(Lleaves), length(Rleaves),
                   dimnames = list(Lleaves, Rleaves))
    ptrB <- matrix(NA_integer_, length(Lleaves), length(Rleaves))
    ptrC <- matrix(NA_integer_, length(Lleaves), length(Rleaves))
    for (ui in seq_along(Lleaves)) {
      u <- Lleaves[ui]
      Lrow <- L_full[as.character(u), ]
      for (wi in seq_along(Rleaves)) {
        w <- Rleaves[wi]
        Rcol <- R_full[, as.character(w)]
        best <- Inf; bestB <- NA_integer_; bestC <- NA_integer_
        for (bi in seq_along(Lleaves)) {
          Lcost <- Lrow[bi]
          if (!is.finite(Lcost)) next
          b <- Lleaves[bi]
          total_vec <- Lcost + Rcol + d[as.character(b), as.character(Rleaves)]
          ci <- which.min(total_vec)
          if (total_vec[ci] < best) { best <- total_vec[ci]; bestB <- b; bestC <- Rleaves[ci] }
        }
        tab[ui, wi] <- best; ptrB[ui, wi] <- bestB; ptrC[ui, wi] <- bestC
      }
    }
    res <- list(leaves = c(Lleaves, Rleaves), table = tab,
                Lleaves = Lleaves, Rleaves = Rleaves,
                ptrB = ptrB, ptrC = ptrC, left = left, right = right)
    memo[[node]] <<- res
    res
  }
  root <- unique(setdiff(phy$edge[, 1], phy$edge[, 2]))
  stopifnot(length(root) == 1)
  top <- dp(root)
  get_order <- function(node_res, start, end) {
    if (length(node_res$leaves) == 1) return(node_res$leaves)
    Lleaves <- node_res$Lleaves; Rleaves <- node_res$Rleaves
    if (start %in% Lleaves && end %in% Rleaves) {
      ui <- match(start, Lleaves); wi <- match(end, Rleaves)
      b <- node_res$ptrB[ui, wi]; c_ <- node_res$ptrC[ui, wi]
      c(get_order(node_res$left, start, b), get_order(node_res$right, c_, end))
    } else if (start %in% Rleaves && end %in% Lleaves) {
      rev(get_order(node_res, end, start))
    } else stop("invalid boundary pair")
  }
  min_cost <- min(top$table)
  idx <- which(top$table == min_cost, arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
  best_order <- get_order(top, top$Lleaves[idx[1]], top$Rleaves[idx[2]])
  list(order = as.integer(best_order), cost = min_cost)
}

make_trait_dist_2 <- function(traits, phy, method = "euclidean", scale_traits = TRUE) {
  stopifnot(all(phy$tip.label %in% rownames(traits)))
  traits <- traits[phy$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]
  if (scale_traits) traits <- scale(traits)
  d <- as.matrix(dist(traits, method = method))
  rownames(d) <- colnames(d) <- as.character(seq_len(nrow(d)))
  d
}

# Local layout helpers (self-contained, rely only on ape edge matrix)
leaf_order_2 <- function(phy) {
  n <- length(phy$tip.label)
  phy$tip.label[phy$edge[phy$edge[, 2] <= n, 2]]
}

layout_cost_2 <- function(phy, traits) {
  ord <- leaf_order_2(phy)
  X <- traits[ord, , drop = FALSE]
  sum(sqrt(rowSums(diff(X)^2)))
}

# =============================================================================
# MAIN FUNCTION
# =============================================================================
interactive_tree_viz <- function(
    tree,                       # ape::phylo object
    traits,                     # numeric matrix, rownames == tree$tip.label
    reorder_olo = TRUE,         # reorder with OLO (Bar-Joseph) before plotting
    scale_traits = TRUE,        # scale traits for the OLO distance / cost readout
    output_file = "interactive_tree.html",
    title = NULL,
    save_newick = NULL,         # optional path to write the (possibly reordered) tree
    selfcontained = TRUE        # inline plotly.js bundle in the HTML
) {
  for (p in c("ape", "plotly", "htmlwidgets", "jsonlite")) {
    if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE))
      stop("Package '", p, "' is required.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!inherits(tree, "phylo")) stop("'tree' must be an ape 'phylo' object.")
  if (is.data.frame(traits)) {
    if (!all(vapply(traits, is.numeric, logical(1))))
      stop("'traits' must be numeric.")
    traits <- as.matrix(traits)
  }
  if (!is.matrix(traits)) stop("'traits' must be a numeric matrix or data.frame.")
  missing_tips <- setdiff(tree$tip.label, rownames(traits))
  if (length(missing_tips))
    stop("Traits missing for tip(s): ", paste(missing_tips, collapse = ", "))
  n <- length(tree$tip.label)
  if (n < 2) stop("Tree must have at least 2 tips.")
  traits <- traits[tree$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]
  if (is.null(title)) title <- "Interactive phylogenetic tree + trait heatmap"
  if (is.null(colnames(traits))) colnames(traits) <- paste0("Trait", seq_len(ncol(traits)))

  # scale guard: constant columns produce NaN after scale()
  if (scale_traits) {
    sds <- apply(traits, 2, stats::sd)
    if (any(!is.finite(sds) | sds == 0)) {
      warning("Constant trait column(s) detected; disabling scaling for OLO.", call. = FALSE)
      scale_traits <- FALSE
    }
  }

  olo_order <- NULL
  cost_mat  <- traits
  out_cost  <- layout_cost_2(tree, traits)

  if (reorder_olo) {
    if (!requireNamespace("ape", quietly = TRUE)) stop("ape required for OLO.")
    node_counts <- table(tree$edge[, 1])
    if (any(node_counts > 2))
      stop("OLO requires a fully bifurcating tree; resolve polytomies with ape::multi2di().")
    d <- make_trait_dist_2(traits, tree, method = "euclidean", scale_traits = scale_traits)
    res <- olo_phylo_2(tree, d)
    ord_labels <- tree$tip.label[res$order]
    # topology-preserving rotation into the OLO-optimal layout
    tree <- ape::rotateConstr(tree, ord_labels)
    olo_order <- ord_labels
    cost_mat  <- if (scale_traits) scale(traits) else traits
    out_cost  <- res$cost
    cat("OLO minimal adjacent trait-dissimilarity:", out_cost, "\n")
  }

  if (!is.null(save_newick)) {
    ape::write.tree(tree, file = save_newick)
    cat("Step tree written to:", save_newick, "\n")
  }

  # ----- serialize tree structure + data for the browser -----
  children <- get_children_list_2(tree)
  n_node <- tree$Nnode
  node_count <- n + n_node
  edge_len <- rep(1, node_count)
  if (!is.null(tree$edge.length)) edge_len[tree$edge[, 2]] <- tree$edge.length
  root <- unique(setdiff(tree$edge[, 1], tree$edge[, 2]))

  # only internal nodes are rotatable -> send those (tips have no children)
  child_map <- list()
  for (nd in (n + 1):node_count) child_map[[as.character(nd)]] <- children[[nd]]
  root <- root[1]

  payload <- list(
    tips       = tree$tip.label,
    children   = child_map,
    edgeLen    = as.list(stats::setNames(edge_len, as.character(seq_len(node_count)))),
    root       = root,
    nodeCount  = node_count,
    traits     = lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) as.numeric(traits[i, ])),
    traitNames = colnames(traits),
    costMat    = lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) as.numeric(cost_mat[i, ])),
    oloOrder   = olo_order,
    title      = title
  )
  payload_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(payload, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = NA)

  # ----- build the plotly htmlwidget -----
  # NOTE: the raw string below uses the '-' delimiter. '|' is NOT a valid R
  # raw-string delimiter: r"|( ... )|" keeps the opening '(' in the value and
  # silently breaks the generated JavaScript.
  .js_body <- r"-(
var TD = __PAYLOAD__;
var tips = TD.tips;
var children = TD.children;
var edgeLen = TD.edgeLen;
var root = TD.root;
var traitsHeat = TD.traits;
var traitsCost = TD.costMat || TD.traits;
var tNames = TD.traitNames;
var n = tips.length;
var oloOrder = TD.oloOrder || null;
var ttl = TD.title || "Phylogenetic tree";

var rev = {};
function initRev(){ rev = {}; for (var k in children) rev[k] = false; }
initRev();

function leafOrder(r){
  var order = [];
  (function dfs(node){
    var ch = children[node];
    if(!ch){ order.push(node*1); return; }
    var kk = r[node] ? ch.slice().reverse() : ch;
    for(var i=0;i<kk.length;i++) dfs(kk[i]);
  })(root);
  return order;
}

function leafCount(node){
  var ch = children[node];
  if(!ch) return 1;
  var s = 0;
  for(var i=0;i<ch.length;i++) s += leafCount(ch[i]);
  return s;
}

function layoutCalc(r){
  var order = leafOrder(r);
  var y = {}, slot = {};
  for(var i=0;i<order.length;i++){ slot[order[i]] = i+1; y[order[i]] = i+1; }
  var mn = {}, mx = {};
  (function ranges(node){
    var ch = children[node];
    if(!ch){ mn[node]=slot[node]; mx[node]=slot[node]; return; }
    var lo = Infinity, hi = -Infinity;
    for(var i=0;i<ch.length;i++){
      ranges(ch[i]);
      if(mn[ch[i]] < lo) lo = mn[ch[i]];
      if(mx[ch[i]] > hi) hi = mx[ch[i]];
    }
    mn[node] = lo; mx[node] = hi;
    y[node] = (lo + hi) / 2;
  })(root);
  var x = {}; x[root] = 0;
  (function xs(node){
    var ch = children[node] || [];
    for(var i=0;i<ch.length;i++){
      x[ch[i]] = x[node] + (edgeLen[ch[i]] || 1);
      xs(ch[i]);
    }
  })(root);
  return {x:x, y:y, order:order};
}

function edgeTrace(L){
  var ex = [], ey = [];
  (function go(node){
    var ch = children[node] || [];
    for(var i=0;i<ch.length;i++){
      var c = ch[i];
      ex.push(L.x[node], L.x[c], null); ey.push(L.y[node], L.y[node], null);
      ex.push(L.x[c], L.x[c], null);    ey.push(L.y[node], L.y[c], null);
      go(c);
    }
  })(root);
  return {type:"scatter", mode:"lines", x:ex, y:ey,
          line:{color:"#8a8a8a", width:1.4}, hoverinfo:"skip", showlegend:false};
}

function tipTrace(L, showLabels){
  var x=[], y=[], txt=[];
  L.order.forEach(function(t){ x.push(L.x[t]); y.push(L.y[t]); txt.push(tips[t-1]); });
  var tr = {type:"scatter", mode:"markers", x:x, y:y, text:txt,
            hovertemplate:"<b>%{text}</b><extra>tip</extra>",
            marker:{size:7, color:"#1f77b4", line:{width:1, color:"#ffffff"}},
            showlegend:false};
  if(showLabels !== false && n <= 40){ tr.mode = "markers+text"; tr.textposition = "middle right"; tr.textfont = {size:10}; }
  return tr;
}

function intTrace(L){
  var x=[], y=[], cd=[], tt=[];
  var keys = [];
  for(var k in children) keys.push(+k);
  keys.sort(function(a,b){ return a-b; });
  keys.forEach(function(nd){
    x.push(L.x[nd]); y.push(L.y[nd]); cd.push(nd);
    tt.push(leafCount(nd) + " tips in this clade - click to rotate");
  });
  return {type:"scatter", mode:"markers", x:x, y:y, customdata:cd, text:tt,
          hovertemplate:"<b>Internal node %{customdata}</b><br>%{text}<extra></extra>",
          marker:{symbol:"diamond", size:9, color:"#e08a1e", line:{width:1, color:"#9a5a00"}},
          showlegend:false};
}

function heatTrace(L){
  var Z = [];
  L.order.forEach(function(t){ Z.push(traitsHeat[t-1]); });
  return {type:"heatmap", z:Z,
          y:L.order.map(function(t){ return tips[t-1]; }),
          x:tNames, xaxis:"x2", yaxis:"y2",
          colorscale:"Viridis",
          colorbar:{thickness:10, len:0.6, y:0.5, title:{text:"value"}},
          hovertemplate:"<b>%{y}</b><br>%{x}: %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>",
          showlegend:false};
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Second view: tree + species names + selected trait values (composite panels)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
var viewMode = "heat";   // "heat" = tree + heatmap, "trait" = tree + names + values
var traitIdx = 0;

function traitValues(){
  return traitsHeat.map(function(row){ return row[traitIdx]; });
}

function traitRange(){
  var v = traitValues();
  var lo = Math.min.apply(null, v), hi = Math.max.apply(null, v);
  var pad = (hi - lo) * 0.12;
  if(!(pad > 0)) pad = 0.1;
  return [lo - pad, hi + pad];
}

function labelStride(){
  // keep the species panel readable for large trees: at most ~45 labels
  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / 45));
}

function namesTrace(L){
  var stride = labelStride();
  var x = [], y = [], txt = [];
  L.order.forEach(function(t, i){
    if(i % stride !== 0) return;
    x.push(0.02); y.push(L.y[t]);
    txt.push("<i>" + tips[t-1] + "</i>");
  });
  return {type:"scatter", mode:"text", x:x, y:y, text:txt,
          xaxis:"x2", yaxis:"y",
          textposition:"middle right",
          textfont:{size:10, family:"Times New Roman, Georgia, serif"},
          hovertemplate:"<b>%{text}</b><extra>species</extra>",
          showlegend:false};
}

function guideTrace(L, xr){
  var x = [], y = [];
  L.order.forEach(function(t){
    x.push(xr[0], xr[1], null);
    y.push(L.y[t], L.y[t], null);
  });
  return {type:"scatter", mode:"lines", x:x, y:y,
          xaxis:"x3", yaxis:"y",
          line:{color:"#d9d9d9", width:0.8, dash:"dot"},
          hoverinfo:"skip", showlegend:false};
}

function valueTrace(L){
  var vals = traitValues();
  var x = [], y = [], txt = [], cd = [];
  L.order.forEach(function(t){
    x.push(vals[t-1]); y.push(L.y[t]);
    txt.push("<i>" + tips[t-1] + "</i>"); cd.push(vals[t-1]);
  });
  return {type:"scatter", mode:"markers", x:x, y:y, text:txt, customdata:cd,
          xaxis:"x3", yaxis:"y",
          hovertemplate:"<b>%{text}</b><br>" + tNames[traitIdx] + ": %{customdata:.3f}<extra>trait</extra>",
          marker:{size:8, color:"#228b22", line:{width:1, color:"#ffffff"}},
          showlegend:false};
}

var lay = {
  title:{text: ttl},
  xaxis:{domain:[0,0.40], showgrid:false, zeroline:false, showticklabels:false},
  yaxis:{domain:[0.05,0.96], range:[0.5,n+0.5], showgrid:false, zeroline:false, showticklabels:false},
  xaxis2:{domain:[0.50,0.90], type:"category", autorange:true, showgrid:false, zeroline:false,
          showticklabels:true, visible:true, title:{text:"Trait"}, tickangle:-30, automargin:true},
  yaxis2:{domain:[0.05,0.96], range:[0.5,n+0.5], visible:true, showgrid:false, showticklabels:false},
  xaxis3:{visible:false},
  annotations:[],
  margin:{l:30,r:20,t:70,b:60},
  showlegend:false, hovermode:"closest"
};

function traitLayout(){
  var xr = traitRange();
  return {
    title:{text: ttl},
    xaxis:{domain:[0,0.34], showgrid:false, zeroline:false, showticklabels:false},
    yaxis:{domain:[0.05,0.96], range:[0.5,n+0.5], showgrid:false, zeroline:false, showticklabels:false},
    xaxis2:{domain:[0.36,0.60], range:[0,1], type:"linear", showgrid:false, zeroline:false,
            showticklabels:false, visible:true, title:{text:""}, tickangle:0, automargin:false},
    xaxis3:{domain:[0.68,0.97], range:xr, type:"linear", visible:true, showgrid:true,
            gridcolor:"#efefef", zeroline:false, automargin:true},
    yaxis2:{visible:false},
    annotations:[
      {text:"Phylogenetic tree", xref:"paper", yref:"paper", x:0.17, y:1.02,
       showarrow:false, font:{size:13}},
      {text:"Species" + (labelStride() > 1 ? " (1 in " + labelStride() + ")" : ""),
       xref:"paper", yref:"paper", x:0.48, y:1.02, showarrow:false, font:{size:13}},
      {text:tNames[traitIdx] + " value", xref:"paper", yref:"paper", x:0.825, y:1.02,
       showarrow:false, font:{size:13}}
    ],
    margin:{l:30,r:20,t:90,b:60},
    showlegend:false, hovermode:"closest"
  };
}

var costEl = null;
function updateCost(L){
  var s = 0;
  for(var i=1;i<L.order.length;i++){
    var a = traitsCost[L.order[i-1]-1];
    var b = traitsCost[L.order[i]-1];
    var d2 = 0;
    for(var j=0;j<a.length;j++){ var dd = a[j]-b[j]; d2 += dd*dd; }
    s += Math.sqrt(d2);
  }
  if(costEl) costEl.textContent = s.toFixed(4);
}

function revForTarget(targetLabels){
  var tIdx = {};
  for(var i=0;i<targetLabels.length;i++) tIdx[targetLabels[i]] = i;
  var base = leafOrder({});
  var pos = {};
  base.forEach(function(t){ pos[t] = tIdx[tips[t-1]]; });
  var mn = {};
  (function calc(node){
    var ch = children[node];
    if(!ch){ mn[node] = pos[node]; return; }
    var lo = Infinity;
    for(var i=0;i<ch.length;i++){ calc(ch[i]); if(mn[ch[i]] < lo) lo = mn[ch[i]]; }
    mn[node] = lo;
  })(root);
  var r = {};
  (function orient(node){
    var ch = children[node];
    if(!ch) return;
    if(ch.length === 2) r[node] = mn[ch[1]] < mn[ch[0]];
    for(var i=0;i<ch.length;i++) orient(ch[i]);
  })(root);
  return r;
}

function redraw(){
  var L = layoutCalc(rev);
  if(viewMode === "trait"){
    Plotly.react(el, [edgeTrace(L), tipTrace(L, false), intTrace(L),
                      namesTrace(L), guideTrace(L, traitRange()), valueTrace(L)],
                 traitLayout());
  } else {
    Plotly.react(el, [edgeTrace(L), tipTrace(L), intTrace(L), heatTrace(L)], lay);
  }
  updateCost(L);
}

var ui = document.createElement("div");
ui.style.cssText = "font-family:-apple-system,Segoe UI,Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:13px;padding:6px 2px;line-height:1.7;";
var html = "<b>Adjacent trait distance:</b> <span style=\"color:#1f77b4;font-weight:700\" id=\"olocostLbl\">0</span>";
html += "<button id=\"oloresetBtn\" style=\"margin-left:16px\">Reset</button>";
if(oloOrder){ html += " <button id=\"olobestBtn\" title=\"Apply the OLO-optimal tip order\">Apply OLO-optimal order</button>"; }
html += " <button id=\"traitViewBtn\" title=\"Toggle the species + trait value panels\">Species + trait panel</button>";
var opts = "";
for(var i=0;i<tNames.length;i++){ opts += "<option value=\"" + i + "\">" + tNames[i] + "</option>"; }
html += " <span id=\"traitSelWrap\" style=\"margin-left:10px;display:none\">trait: <select id=\"traitSel\">" + opts + "</select></span>";
html += "&nbsp; <span style=\"color:#777\">Click a <b style=\"color:#e08a1e\">diamond</b> (internal node) to flip its two child clades. Hover tips, internal nodes, heatmap cells, or trait dots for details.</span>";
ui.innerHTML = html;
el.parentNode.insertBefore(ui, el);
costEl = document.getElementById("olocostLbl");
document.getElementById("oloresetBtn").addEventListener("click", function(){ initRev(); redraw(); });
if(oloOrder){
  document.getElementById("olobestBtn").addEventListener("click", function(){ rev = revForTarget(oloOrder); redraw(); });
}
var traitViewBtn = document.getElementById("traitViewBtn");
var traitSelWrap  = document.getElementById("traitSelWrap");
var traitSel      = document.getElementById("traitSel");
traitViewBtn.addEventListener("click", function(){
  viewMode = (viewMode === "trait") ? "heat" : "trait";
  traitViewBtn.textContent = (viewMode === "trait") ? "Back to heatmap view" : "Species + trait panel";
  traitSelWrap.style.display = (viewMode === "trait") ? "inline" : "none";
  redraw();
});
traitSel.addEventListener("change", function(){ traitIdx = +traitSel.value; redraw(); });

el.on("plotly_click", function(data){
  var pts = data.points || [];
  for(var i=0;i<pts.length;i++){
    var p = pts[i];
    if(p.curveNumber === 2 && p.customdata !== undefined){
      var node = p.customdata;
      rev[node] = !rev[node];
      redraw();
      return;
    }
  }
});

redraw();
)-"

  js_full <- gsub("__PAYLOAD__", payload_json, .js_body, fixed = TRUE)

  fig <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(plotly::plot_ly()))
  widget <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    htmlwidgets::onRender(fig, paste0("function(el, x) {\n", js_full, "\n}"))
  ))
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    htmlwidgets::saveWidget(widget, output_file, selfcontained = selfcontained)
  ))

  cat("Saved interactive tree visualization to:", output_file, "\n")

  invisible(list(
    tree  = tree,
    order = leaf_order_2(tree),
    cost  = out_cost,
    olo   = olo_order,
    file  = output_file,
    widget = widget
  ))
}
```

```{r interactive-tree-viz-demo}
# Build the interactive widget from the experimental objects of this report.
# (Requires 'my_tree' and 'traits' created upstream by 02_reorder.Rmd.)
stopifnot(exists("my_tree", inherits = TRUE), exists("traits", inherits = TRUE))

if (any(table(my_tree$edge[, 1]) > 2)) {
  my_tree <- ape::multi2di(my_tree)
  message("Polytomies resolved with ape::multi2di() before OLO reordering.")
}

res_viz <- interactive_tree_viz(
  tree         = my_tree,
  traits       = traits,
  reorder_olo  = TRUE,
  scale_traits = TRUE,
  output_file  = "interactive_tree_heatmap.html",
  title        = "Interactive phylogenetic tree + trait heatmap (OLO-optimal order)",
  save_newick  = "interactive_tree_heatmap.tre"
)

# --- self-check: the file exists and the returned order is a valid layout ----
stopifnot(file.exists(res_viz$file))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sort(res_viz$order), sort(my_tree$tip.label))))
cat("OLO-optimal tip order (first 10):", paste(head(res_viz$olo, 10), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("OLO cost (scaled traits):", round(res_viz$cost, 4), "\n")
cat("Interactive widget written to:", res_viz$file, "\n")

res_viz$widget
```
